title: Responsive images and typography
learningObjectives: Explain responsive images and typography and apply responsive design principles.

understand.concept: Responsive images can use flexible CSS sizing, srcset and sizes for resolution selection, and picture with source elements for art direction. Responsive typography can use fluid values, sensible limits, and readable line lengths.
understand.whyItMatters: Images that overflow can break layouts or force scrolling. Typography that scales without limits can become too small or too large. Test real content and preserve meaningful image alternatives.
understand.analogy: Responsive images choose a suitable source and size for the viewing context; responsive text adjusts while staying within readable limits.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; responsive behaviour is determined by CSS layout and viewport/container conditions.

explain.narrative: The picture element can select a different source at a media condition; the img remains the fallback and carries the alt text.

examples.code: Text with a fluid size and comfortable line height.
examples.explanation: The picture element can select a different source at a media condition; the img remains the fallback and carries the alt text.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the responsive behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Use srcset and sizes for resolution switching or picture for art direction. Add fluid typography with clamp() and test narrow screens.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive page section and test it at narrow, medium, and wide viewport sizes, including longer labels.
hints: Use the browser responsive viewport tools.
Check horizontal overflow and text scaling.
Keep keyboard access and semantic structure intact.

questions.prompt: Which element can select different image sources for art direction?
questions.explanation: picture and its source children allow art direction based on media conditions.

questions.prompt: What should be included in responsive testing?
options: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.answer: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.explanation: Responsive defects often appear at intermediate widths or with expanded content.
